headline: GOLD CLAWS BACK TO $4,050 AFTER FIRST $4,000 BREACH SINCE NOVEMBER — FED CHAIR WARSH WITHHOLDS RATE DOT FOR FIRST TIME IN 14 YEARS; DECEMBER HIKE 80% PRICED
snippet: Spot gold recovered to approximately $4,050–$4,081 on June 26 after briefly breaking below $4,000 for the first time since November 2025 the previous session — ending the week down nearly 5% in its worst five-day stretch of 2026. The primary driver was the Federal Reserve's June FOMC meeting, where nine of 18 members projected at least one rate hike before year-end; Chair Kevin Warsh withheld his own interest rate projection from the dot plot for the first time in 14 years, amplifying uncertainty rather than resolving it. CME FedWatch priced an 80% probability of a December hike and approximately 63% for September. Silver slid to a 7-month low near $57–$59/oz, widening the gold-silver ratio back toward 70:1 from below 50:1 at the January 2026 peak.

headline: ALAN GREENSPAN, 100, DEAD — THE GOLD STANDARD'S MOST FAMOUS ADVOCATE SPENT 18 YEARS AS FED CHAIR CREATING THE EASY MONEY HE ONCE CONDEMNED
source_name: Stefan Gleason / Money Metals Exchange (via GATA)
snippet: Alan Greenspan, former Chairman of the Federal Reserve and one of the most influential economists of the 20th century, died at the age of 100. The gold community is marking his passing with profound ambivalence: in 1966 Greenspan wrote 'Gold and Economic Freedom,' one of the most articulate modern defences of the gold standard, arguing it was the only barrier against the welfare-state confiscation of wealth through inflation. Yet as Fed Chairman from 1987–2006 he presided over the creation of the 'Greenspan put,' persistently easy monetary conditions, and the expansion of the very credit-creation machinery he once condemned. Money Metals Exchange's Stefan Gleason, in a piece published June 26, memorialized him as 'the schizophrenic gold bug' — a man who understood gold's monetary role yet abandoned those principles at the precise moment he had the power to act on them. His legacy remains one of the most contested in monetary history.

headline: F4/URANIUMX EXPAND MURPHY LAKE 60% TO 4,000m — EVERY TARGET RETURNS ANOMALOUS RADIOACTIVITY; 5KM FROM ISOENERGY HURRICANE DEPOSIT (TSXV:FFU / CSE:STMN)
source_name: Junior Mining Network / F4 Uranium Corp. (TSXV:FFU) / UraniumX Discovery Corp. (CSE:STMN)
snippet: F4 Uranium Corp. (TSXV:FFU) and UraniumX Discovery Corp. (CSE:STMN) announced a 60% expansion of the Murphy Lake drill program in the northeastern Athabasca Basin, Saskatchewan — increasing planned metres from 2,500 to 4,000 after seven completed holes confirmed anomalous radioactivity in 100% of target areas tested. Highlight hole ML26-021 returned elevated radioactivity up to 350 cps over 1.0m in basement rocks below the unconformity, alongside strong limonite, bleaching, and clay alteration in the overlying sandstone — the alteration footprint characteristic of fault-controlled uranium systems. The 609-hectare Murphy Lake property sits 5km south of IsoEnergy's high-grade Hurricane Uranium Deposit within one of the world's premier uranium corridors. F4 is the operator; UraniumX is earning up to 70% of the project under the existing option agreement.

headline: EAGLE PLAINS / XCITE FLAG URANIUM CONDUCTOR TARGETS AT DON LAKE & SMITTY ON BLACK BAY FAULT — Q3/Q4 DRILLING PLANNED (TSXV:EPL / TSXV:XRI)
source_name: Stockhouse / Eagle Plains Resources Ltd. (TSXV:EPL) / Xcite Uranium Inc. (TSXV:XRI)
snippet: Eagle Plains Resources (TSXV:EPL) and Xcite Uranium (TSXV:XRI) released June 25 the initial interpretation of a 2025 VTEM Plus airborne geophysical survey covering the Don Lake (1,671 ha) and Smitty (2,384 ha) uranium projects near Uranium City, Saskatchewan. Advanced modelling by Condor Consulting Inc. identified multiple EM conductors aligned parallel to the regional Black Bay Fault — one of the primary structural controls for uranium mineralisation in the historic Beaverlodge camp — and an additional high-conductivity feature in the western Smitty ground beyond the historic mine that will be evaluated during summer fieldwork. Drill targeting is being finalised for a Q3/Q4 2026 program; both projects host near-surface uranium mineralisation and past-producing mines from the Beaverlodge district's operating era.

headline: BRUNSWICK DOUBLES NUUK LITHIUM CORRIDOR TO 4KM IN GREENLAND — SOLE LITHIUM EXPLORER IN COUNTRY; 9 SPODUMENE PEGMATITES SOME 400M x 40M (TSXV:BRW)
snippet: Brunswick Exploration (TSXV:BRW) announced June 24 that field work at its Nuuk Lithium Project near Nuuk, Greenland extended the spodumene-bearing corridor by confirming an additional pegmatite zone more than 3km from the initial discovery — nearly doubling the system to approximately 4km × 1km. A total of nine spodumene-bearing LCT pegmatites have been documented in the Ivisaartoq field, with some measuring up to 400m × 40m and containing up to 50% visual spodumene — dimensions comparable to early surface expressions of larger Greenlandic pegmatite systems. Brunswick is the only company conducting lithium exploration in Greenland, a NATO-aligned jurisdiction entirely outside China's lithium supply chain that has attracted growing critical mineral strategy interest. A maiden drill program is under evaluation alongside return drilling at the Mirage project and a new East Greenland portfolio prospecting campaign beginning mid-July.

headline: SECTION 232 COPPER REPORT DUE MONDAY — COMEX HITS RECORD 650,000t AS HUDBAY, FREEPORT BRACE FOR BINARY TARIFF EVENT; GOLDMAN TARGETS $14,000+/t IF 30% DUTY PROCEEDS
snippet: The US Commerce Department's mandated Section 232 report on copper market security — which will determine whether the President moves to impose phased tariffs of 15% from 2027 and 30% from 2028 on refined copper imports — is due to the White House on Monday, June 30, 2026. COMEX copper inventories have surged to a record 650,000 tonnes as manufacturers and traders front-run any tariff announcement, creating a two-sided price risk: the build weighs on near-term prices but could reverse sharply once tariff certainty arrives. Goldman Sachs forecasts copper could breach $14,000/tonne under a 30% tariff scenario materialising in 2028; near-term, the bank projects LME prices at $13,000–$13,500. Hudbay Minerals (NYSE:HBM), Freeport-McMoRan (NYSE:FCX), and Ivanhoe Electric (TSX:IE) are among the copper producers with the most direct exposure to the US market pricing outcome.

headline: HEAVY RARE EARTHS SURGE: TERBIUM +22.8% IN JUNE 2026, GERMANIUM AT RECORD $2,673/KG AS BEIJING EXPORT LICENSING TIGHTENS CRITICAL SUPPLY TO THE WEST
snippet: The June 2026 rare earth market has seen heavy rare earth prices rebound sharply, with terbium as the standout performer at +22.8% month-to-date — the largest single-month gain for the element in over two years. Germanium, a semiconductor and defense-optics critical material processed almost entirely in China, reached a new 2026 domestic high of $2,673.66/kg, up approximately 30% from April's $2,049/kg, driven by Beijing's export licensing scheme that has severely constrained flows to Western processors. The heavy rare earth surge comes as Energy Fuels' White Mesa Mill — the only facility in the US capable of processing a full suite of rare earth oxides alongside uranium — prepares to switch to commercial heavy REE circuit production starting in July, underscoring how thin Western rare earth processing capacity remains even at record incentive prices.

headline: GOLDSEEK COT JUNE 26: SPECULATOR GOLD LONGS REDUCED AS DOLLAR HITS 1-YEAR HIGH — POSITIONING DATA WATCHED FOR SIGNALS OF A TECHNICAL FLOOR
snippet: GoldSeek's weekly Commitment of Traders analysis for gold, silver, and the US dollar index was published June 26, covering COMEX futures positions through Tuesday June 23. The weekly COT report is closely watched by mining investors as a leading sentiment indicator — historically, significant reductions in managed-money net long positions alongside narrowing commercial net short exposure have preceded meaningful bounces in both spot gold and mining equities. With gold having fallen to multi-month lows as Fed rate-hike odds pushed the dollar to its highest level in over a year, the June 26 positioning snapshot provides the first week-ending read on whether speculative unwinding is approaching levels associated with prior technical bottoms, or whether additional liquidation pressure remains ahead of the June 30 Section 232 copper decision and month-end window dressing.

headline: BANK GOLD FORECASTS DIVERGE $1,700 — MACQUARIE CUTS TO $4,300 WHILE JPM HOLDS $6,000, GOLDMAN $4,900 AS RATE-HIKE CONSENSUS HARDENS
snippet: With gold entering the June 27 weekend near $4,050 after its worst week of 2026, analyst year-end forecasts reveal an unusually wide $1,700 divergence: Macquarie has trimmed its year-end target to $4,300/oz, while J.P. Morgan holds its $6,000 forecast, Goldman Sachs marks $4,900, and UBS sits near $5,900. The spread reflects genuinely different assumptions about Fed policy follow-through — Macquarie's cut prices in the dot-plot hawkishness as real, while JPM's hold reflects conviction that the US fiscal trajectory (debt/GDP above 130%) is not resolved by one or two hikes and that structural central bank buying will absorb speculative selling. Physical gold investment demand reached a 50% year-on-year increase in Q1 2026 even as spot prices corrected, suggesting accumulation rather than distribution by the most patient buyers.

headline: WORST WEEK OF 2026 FOR GOLD: DOWN ~5%, SILVER AT 7-MONTH LOW, GOLD/SILVER RATIO WIDENS TOWARD 70:1 AS FED HIKE BETS SOAR
snippet: Gold posted its worst weekly performance of 2026, losing approximately 5% as the Federal Reserve's hawkish June FOMC outcome reverberated through the metals complex — Fed Chair Warsh's decision to withhold his own rate projection from the dot plot for the first time in 14 years, combined with nine of 18 members projecting at least one additional hike, drove the dollar to its highest point in over a year. Silver fell more sharply in percentage terms, reaching a 7-month low near $57/oz, with the gold-silver ratio widening back toward 70:1 from below 50:1 at the January 2026 peak — a level historically associated with silver's most explosive subsequent outperformance when momentum reverses. China's January 2026 reclassification of silver as a strategic material and the resulting export licensing restrictions have reduced the ability of physical flows to cushion paper selling.

headline: GDX HITS RECORD FCF YIELD AND 5-YEAR LOW FORWARD P/E DURING GOLD CORRECTION — ANALYSTS FLAG BEST MINER ENTRY POINT OF THE 2026 BULL MARKET
snippet: While gold's spot price has corrected approximately 27% from its January 28, 2026 all-time high of $5,589/oz to near $4,050, the VanEck Gold Miners ETF (GDX) is generating record free cash flow at current prices — a paradox explained by historically wide miner margins of approximately $2,800/oz even after the correction. A widely-discussed June 2026 Seeking Alpha analysis presenting six valuation charts argues that GDX's forward P/E has fallen to a five-year low and its free-cash-flow-to-EV yield sits at a record high, creating a risk/reward profile rarely seen during a structurally intact bull market. Options flows on GDX have leaned bullish even on sessions where gold itself fell, with call volumes outpacing puts by as much as 5:1 at peak, suggesting institutional positioning ahead of a miner multiple re-rating if the rate-hike scare resolves.
